alkylation_concentration.evidence: Each protein sample was diluted to a final concentration of 2 μg/μl, reduced with 10 mM DTT at 56°C for 1 hour, and alkylated with 20 mM IAA in the dark at room temperature for 1 hour.

alkylation_reagent.evidence: Each protein sample was diluted to a final concentration of 2 μg/μl, reduced with 10 mM DTT at 56°C for 1 hour, and alkylated with 20 mM IAA in the dark at room temperature for 1 hour.

cleavage_agent.evidence: The proteins were then digested overnight at 37°C with sequencing-grade porcine trypsin at a 1:20 enzyme-to-substrate ratio in 300 μl of 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate.

Briefly, the Trypsin/P was used as a cleavage rule with up to 2 missed cleavages; “Carbamidomethyl(C)” was set as a fixed modification, and “Acetyl (Protein N-term)” and “Oxidation(M)” were set as variable modifications; Top3-6 Best N Fragments per peptide were enabled.

labeling.evidence: Sample sets Fibroblast pSILAC sample set (2-channel pSILAC). The skin fibroblast cell lines were purchased from the Coriell Institute for Medical Research.

Measuring protein turnover is essential for understanding cellular biological processes and advancing drug discovery. The multiplex-DIA mass spectrometry (DIA-MS) approach, combined with dynamic SILAC labeling (pulse-SILAC, or pSILAC), has proven to be a reliable method for analyzing protein turnover and degradation kinetics.
